messages:
maria: Quick sync — we need a short decision on the TTL for degrade notifications from the auto-fallback policy. Current impl fires a notification every time a request triggers fallback; infra costs and pager noise are getting bad. Thoughts?

raj: Ugh yeah, saw the spike in alerts this morning. We probably want dedupe TTL per route + per-degrade-reason. e.g. 10m per route, 1h per customer?

ev an: @raj per-customer TTL sounds dangerous for multi-tenant hosts. If a single customer triggers a noisy cascade we still want an operator backstop. Maybe a global rate cap on notifications and a per-route suppression window.

sophie: Agree with evan. Proposal: 1) dedupe window = 10m per route+reason, 2) global daily cap per workspace (configurable), 3) operator backstop alert when suppressed hits threshold.

maria: That seems sensible. How do we surface that in the Console and API? Users will expect to opt into less noisy notifications.

raj: Console UX: simple slider or numeric field for "degrade notification TTL (route-level)" + toggle for "enable global backstop alerts". Default to conservative. API: add fields to rollout policy object: `notification_ttl_seconds`, `global_notification_cap_per_day`, `backstop_threshold_count`.

sophie: Rough schema snippet (for backend/API):
```json
{"policy_id": "string", "degrade_rules": [{"id":"r1","reason":"kv_cache_miss","notification_ttl_seconds":600}], "notification_caps": {"global_cap_per_workspace":1000, "backstop_threshold":50}}
```

evan: Two operational concerns: 1) telemetry sampling for audit — if we suppress notifications, we still need to log every fallback event for forensic/replay. 2) retention: store raw fallback events for X days and aggregated telemetry for longer.

maria: Good call — let's keep raw events for 30d and aggregated counts for 1y by default. Sophie, can we make that part of the rollout policy or is that infra config?

sophie: Raw retention sits in the ingest pipeline config (infra). But policy can opt-in to extended retention per-customer (enterprise). We'll expose `audit_retention_days` on Enterprise rollouts.

raj: UX detail — when notifications are suppressed, Console should show a badge on route with "suppressed N events (last 10m)" so users can drill into raw events. That avoids surprise.

maria: Also need to include degrade reason codes in webhook payloads so downstream systems can filter. E.g. `DEGRADE_KV_MISS`, `DEGRADE_OVERLOAD`, `DEGRADE_MODEL_FALLBACK`.

sophie: I'll add those to the API contract. Quick example payload: 
```json
{"event_type":"fallback","route":"/v1/generate","reason":"DEGRADE_KV_MISS","ts":1650000000,"suppressed":false}
```

ops-bot: [alert] autofallback-suppression-trigger workspace=acme corp route=/v1/generate suppressed_count=42

evan: ops-bot sample confirms the noise. We should also implement exponential backoff for notifications on persistent issues rather than flat TTL. E.g. 10m -> 30m -> 2h -> 1d per route+reason.

raj: Exponential sequence makes sense. Need to expose at least the base and multiplier in policy. Keep sane defaults in Console.

maria: Ownership: Sophie - update API contract + Console mockups; Evan - define alerting/backstop thresholds and telemetry sampling; Raj - write small product blurb for defaults. I'll draft RFC by EOD.

sophie: On it. Will put a draft PR with schema & Console wireframes.

ev an: I'll stub alert playbook for the operator backstop (who to page, runbook link).

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: feature/autofallback-notify-ttl -> staging (sha: bc1234).

maria: Nice. One more: can we include an audit toggle to replay suppressed events to the user's webhook during a maintenance window? That'd help postmortems.

sophie: Good idea — add `replay_suppressed_events: {enabled: bool, window_days: int}` to enterprise policy. I'll include in API draft.

raj: +1. If we can surface replay status in Console that will be huge for customers.

maria: OK team — thanks. If no objections I'll merge the RFC after Sophie/Evan push PRs. :thumbsup:
